Opposite Parties ---
CORAM: HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE RONGON MUKHOPADHYAY ---
For the Petitioner : Mr. Rohitabh Das, Advocate For the State : Mr. Shekhar Sinha, APP  ---
Order No. 08 Dated 03rd October, 2018 Heard Mr. Rohitabh Das, learned counsel for the petitioner and Mr. Shekhar Sinha, learned APP for the State.
In this application the petitioner has prayed for quashing of the entire criminal proceeding in connection with Case No. C IV 02/2007 including the order dated 03.07.2007 passed by learned Sub Divisional Judicial Magistrate, Ranchi by which cognizance has been taken for the offences punishable u/s 16(1)(a)(i) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954.
Learned counsel for the petitioner at the outset submits that the case of one of the co-accused has already been quashed in Cr.M.P. No. 1374 of 2010.

It has further been submitted that there has been sufficient compliance of Rule 32 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Rules and on such score the case of the other co-accused person has been quashed by this Court.
Learned APP appearing for the State has opposed the prayer made by the petitioner.
It appears that the petitioner was the then Branch Manager, I.T.C. Limited who has been prosecuted for commission of the offence u/s 16(1)(a)(i) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: powder was not labeled in accordance with the requirements of Rule 32(1) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Rules i.e. best before use is written in small letters and as per rule, the month and year should be mentioned in capital letters and hence it was misbranded which invites prosecution u/s 16(1)(a)(i) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954.

After the prosecution report was submitted, cognizance was taken by the learned Sub Divisional Judicial Magistrate, Ranchi vide order dated 03.07.2007, which is under challenge in the present application.

In the case of Jalaj Kumar Chatterjee in Cr.M.P. No. 1377 of 2010, order dated 06.02.2013 was passed by this Court, relevant portion of which reads as follows:-
"Misbranded has been defined in Section 2(ix) of the Act, which reads as follows:-
(ix) "misbranded"- an article of food shall be deemed to be misbranded (k) if it is not labeled in accordance with the requirements of this Act or rules made thereunder.
Therefore, the case of the prosecution also falls within sub-Section (k) of Section 2(ix) of the Act.
Rule 32 of the Act envisages that month and year upto which the product is best for consumption should be written in the capital letters in the manner indicated below.
"BEST BEFORE ... .... .... MONTH AND YEAR."
It is the case of the prosecution that those words are there over the packet but they are in the small letters.
In that situation, sufficient compliance of the rule seems to be there.
Under such situation, prosecution of the petitioner seems to be unwarranted."

Since it has been held that Best Before and the Month and Year which has been mentioned in small letters on the label was sufficient compliance of Rule 32(1) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Rules and therefore no case of misbranding is made out and since the case of the petitioner is similar to that of the case of Jalaj Kumar Chatterjee (Cr.M.P. No. 1374 of 2010), the entire criminal proceeding in connection with Case No. C IV 02/2007 including the order dated 03.07.2007 passed by learned Sub Divisional Judicial Magistrate, Ranchi by which cognizance has been taken for the offences punishable u/s 16(1)(a)(i) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954, is hereby quashed and set aside so far as the petitioner is concerned.
This application is accordingly allowed.

MK (Rongon Mukhopadhyay, J)
